jobs.description:
The Friedrich Schiller University Jena is a dynamic and innovation-driven university centrally located in Germany. With a broad range of disciplines, it shapes the future through excellent research and teaching. Its scientific excellence is reflected in the profile areas Light - Life - Liberty, which provide pioneering insights and sustainable solutions for the society of tomorrow. Through close collaborations with leading research institutions, innovative companies, and renowned cultural organizations, it advances interdisciplinary developments. With around 17,000 students and approximately 10,000 employees, it defines Jena as a vibrant, internationally connected city of science and innovation.

The Institute of Biodiversity, Ecology and Evolution at the Faculty of Biological Sciences seeks to fill the position of a

Doctoral Researcher in Viral Ecology (m/f/d)

commencing on 01 December 2026. We offer a part-time position (65%, 26 hours per week), with a fixed-term employment until 30 June 2030.

The DFG-funded Collaborative Research Centre 1768 “VirusREvolution: Decoding tools for virus research” is a highly ambitious research centre at Friedrich Schiller University with the joint goal to develop novel tools for virus discovery, characterisation, regulation, interaction, and visualisation (https://virusrevolution.uni-jena.de/). Its integrated research training group is educating doctoral researchers in a structured, interdisciplinary training program and invites applications for doctoral and postdoctoral researcher positions in various fields of research.
In this doctoral project “Do viruses exploit their quasispecies for host range evolution?”, you will investigate how host range and environmental conditions shape virus diversity and virus-host interactions in natural and experimentally manipulated microbial communities.
Conduct experimental work and analyses on virus-host interactions in soil and groundwater ecosystems, including host-range assays, environmental sampling, and targeted microcosm experiments
Analyse metagenomic and viromic data sets from soil and groundwater samples to identify broad- and narrow-host-range viruses to characterize their quasispecies characteristics
Participation in the Collaborative Research Centre VirusREvolution and close collaboration with the tandem project partner
Engage in regular discussions with other group and project members
Collaborate with BSc and MSc students working in associated projects
Publish papers and present your work at national and international scientific meetings

A highly motivated candidate with a Master of Science or equivalent degree in biology, microbiology, microbial ecology, virology, bioinformatics, or a related discipline
Experience in experimental microbiology, microbial ecology, and molecular biological methods; knowledge of sequencing-based bioinformatic approaches (metagenomics, viromics); experience with virus-host interactions are desirable.
Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving
Ability to work independently and in a collaborative team
Excellent skills in English are required, both written and spoken

Embedding in a cross-disciplinary, experienced research group and a large, ambitious research consortium
Affiliation to an Integrated Research Training Group, offering close support and a comprehensive education program for hard skills and transferable skills, supported by the Jena Graduate Academy
A family-friendly working environment with a variety of offers for families
University health promotion and a wide range of university sports activities
Remuneration based on the provisions of the Collective Agreement for the Public Sector of the Federal States (TV-L) up to salary scale E13 - depending on the candidate’s personal qualifications -, including a special annual payment in accordance with the collective agreement.
30 days of vacation per calendar year plus two days off on December 24 and 31

About Us
At betatron bio° we support our clients in developing sophisticated instruments and systems for the life science and diagnostics industries.

Our focus is on microfluidics, systems engineering, and AI - three disciplines we bring together into thoughtfully engineered and integrated systems, taking complex ideas from early concept through prototyping, validation, and pilot production.

To strategically expand our product and systems development in Münster, we are looking for a Senior Electrical Engineer (m/f/d) who will take ownership of the hardware and PCB design for complex measurement and control systems and see projects through from circuit design to final commissioning.

You will work in a highly specialized team with direct customer contact, international project assignments, and a short path from idea to implementation.
Design and develop PCB layouts for analytical instruments, medical-technology and diagnostic systems (analog, digital, mixed-signal) - from concept through to production-ready design
Hardware design including component selection, schematic capture, and design for manufacturability (DFM/DFT)
Develop and integrate firmware (embedded C/C++) for microcontroller-based measurement and control systems
Systematically test, debug, and commission electronic assemblies directly in the lab - hands-on and solution-oriented
System integration in close coordination with mechanical engineers, software developers, and customers
Technical documentation in line with regulatory requirements (IEC 60601, ISO 13485)
Help shape and continuously improve our development processes in a growing deep-tech startup
Must-haves

Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, mechatronics, or related technical field
At least 5+ years of professional experience in PCB design and hardware development - ideally in medtech, diagnostics, or industrial automation
Hands-on firmware development: embedded C/C++, microcontroller programming, interfaces (SPI, I2C, UART, USB)
Hands-on experience with test instruments such as oscilloscopes, signal generators, spectrum analyzers including structured test execution, documentation, and reporting.
Strong ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams and drive independent work.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and in German.

Nice-to-haves

Experience with microfluidic systems, lab-on-chip, or MEMS
Knowledge of EMC-compliant design and signal integrity analysis
Experience with ISO 13485 / IEC 60601 or comparable regulatory frameworks
Knowledge of Python or MATLAB for data analysis and test automation

Real impact: You'll help shape our product architecture directly - your designs go into market-relevant life science devices and directly influence our customers' strategies.

Variety, not routine: Projects spanning multiple customers, applications (diagnostics, single-cell analysis, sequencing, lab automation), and development phases - no two days alike.

Top-tier team: Work alongside internationally experienced founders, AI engineers, and systems engineers.

Growth & responsibility: A clear development path in a fast-growing company - help shape our processes, methods, and team.

Flexibility & culture: Flexible working hours, short decision-making paths, and a collaborative culture (innovation, excellence, collaboration)

Attractive package: Competitive compensation and a modern workplace in the heart of Münster.

About betatron bio°
At betatron bio°, we believe that great engineering happens when deep technical expertise meets speed, curiosity, and practical execution.

We combine deep microfluidics expertise with systems engineering excellence and AI-powered development tools - for results that speak for themselves.

If you want to work on real-world engineering problems with real-world impact, rather than maintaining an established product for years, we would like to hear from you.

jobs.description:
Introduction

The INM-Leibniz Institute for New Materials is an internationally leading center for interdisciplinary research on materials, and their exploitation in materials-based solutions for a sustainable world with increasing digitalization and medical needs. Our research integrates materials chemistry, biological engineering, physical analysis, process engineering and data science. We collaborate with academic and industrial partners all around the world.

A focus of our research are Engineered Living Materials (ELMs), an emergent class of materials from the combination of inert materials and living organism, with huge potential for sustainable innovation in different technological fields. Across the institute, materials scientists, synthetic biologists and biophysicists cooperate to understand living and inert matter, and to realize new materials with unprecedented functions from a synergistic interfacing.

We are strongly linked to collaborative initiatives in the ELM field including the Leibniz ScienceCampus LifeMat, Living Therapeutic Materials, the Priority Program SPP2451 “Living Materials with Adaptive Functions”, and the MaterialVital Hub.

As part of our ELM research community, we are seeking a

Postdoctoral Researcher with expertise in Microbial Biophysics (f/m/d)

with interest in the fundamental understanding of microbial communities within synthetic microenvironments. The candidate will be part of an interdisciplinary research team within the Department Dynamic Biomaterials at INM.

Experimental research to understand microbial behaviour in confined spaces (synthetic hydrogels) and dynamic environments using imaging, microfluidics and molecular biology methods.
Scientific cooperation with researchers in materials science and synthetic biology at INM, and with external partners in bioanalytics/bioinformatics within running funded projects.
Compilation and presentation of research results in the form of progress reports and presentations at project meetings and scientific conferences.
Communication of research results within the scientific community at conferences and scientific events, and publication in scientific journals.
Co-supervision of students and doctoral researchers.
Support and promote the digitalization of ELM research in collaboration with dedicated experts in the group.

PhD degree in biophysics/cell biology or related discipline.
Experience during your PhD or previous postdoctoral stay as experimental researcher in the field of microbial biophysics.
Interest in collaborative and interdisciplinary research challenges.
Self-driven and hands-on personality. Organization and prioritization skills.
Very good communication skills in English.

Work in an emergent research topic, with multiple opportunities to develop a competitive research profile.
An interdisciplinary research environment with complementary expertise and ready to share knowledge and support your work.
State-of-the-art infrastructure, including access to Core Facilities run by experts.
Access to a broad international network with vibrant scientific collaborators and exciting cooperation projects.
A highly professional and supportive working environment with an open and international culture.
A well-structured on-boarding process and clear responsibilities.
Transparent opportunities for career development.
Flexible working hours and mobile working opportunity.
A family-friendly working place.
A EG 13 TV-L position (full time). A part time position is also possible.

The position is initially for 2 years.
